title: 《Journey》开发商 thatgamecompany 宣布推出 thatgamepublisher
content:
Journey maker thatgamecompany announces thatgamepublisher
Business
News
Journey maker thatgamecompany announces thatgamepublisher
Profit from Sky: Children of the Light will support the initiative.
Nicole Carpenter
,
Columnist
,
Game Developer
August 25, 2026
2 Min Read
Via thatgamecompany
Sky: Children of the Light
and
Journey
developer thatgamecompany announced Tuesday it's getting into publishing. The new publishing department, called thatgamepublisher, is investing profit from
Sky: Children of Light
into publishing "emotionally ambitious games,"
according to a report from GamesIndustry.biz
.
Thatgamecompany co-founder Jenova Chen told GamesIndustry.biz that the publishing arm has signed "a couple" games so far. None of them have been released just yet.
"The typical genre or platform restrictions would not apply to us," SJ Xue, who leads the publishing company, told GamesIndustry.biz. "We are open to teams of any size, projects at any stage, and ideas still being prototyped. What matters is not the label, genre, scale, or format, but whether the game reaches for meaningful emotional territory and uses interactivity to take players there."
Xue added thatgamepublisher is open to games of varying scales and budgets—"everyone from solo developers with immense creativity to larger teams with AA-level budgets." Terms of the deals made will vary, he told GamesIndustry.biz. Thatgamepublisher is a "full-service publisher," according to the report, including funding as well as marketing, community, and strategy services. That's in contrast to several other indie-led publishing funds, like
Among Us
maker Innersloth's Outersloth fund
and
Peak
developer Landfall's Evil Landfall
, which both operate strictly as funds, with no promises made for other services.
Related:
Creative Artists Agency spins up indie funding venture Frame1Games
Thatgamecompany is the latest in a wave of indie developers who are spreading the wealth; over the past several years, makers of mega-popular games like
Among Us
,
Peak
, and
Palworld
, and others have started different funding initiatives to invest the profits from their games into other indie studios and makers.
"This is a very common pattern because number one, successful indie games usually are on a shoestring, and if the game becomes very successful, suddenly you have an overflow of cash," Chen told GamesIndustry.biz. "But then, you are a small team [making] games, you don't want to suddenly become a thousands of people company, right? And then you can't really spend the money, so with additional money, where can you invest? You want to invest in something you understand, something you really are familiar with. So investing into other indie games is a natural choice for everyone, and that's why many indie companies are doing that."
